newsitem.title: USA: NY Senate seen unlikely to approve casinos--paper.
newsitem.headline: NY Senate seen unlikely to approve casinos--paper.

text.p: New York State Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, said he considered it increasingly unlikely that the Senate would approve a measure legalizing casino gambling, New York Times reported Thursday.

But the paper said all sides in the fight did not consider the bill dead. Many legsislative officials think it could still be approved if Democrats join the Republican majority in voting in favor of the proposal, the paper said.
If approved by the legislature, the bill then would go to the voters in a referendum.

In 1995, the first time the amendment was voted on, almost all of the Senate Democrats rejected it, but many legislative officials in both parties said "quite a few" Democrats would support it if they were allowed to vote freely by the Senate minority leader, according to the Times.

It added Bruno said he would bring the measure to a vote within three weeks. And if it failed, he would not let the Senate vote on it again this year so that the senators would not be pressured by anti-gambling lobbyists.

The proposal would let casinos be built in Niagara Falls, Buffalo, the Catskills and either Warren or Saratoga counties. It would allow one casino in each of those areas except the Catskills, which could have an unlimited number, according to the paper.
